answer: An agent economy can make influence depend on a bonded stake rather than account count: each identity must lock tokens for a fixed period, and rewards are weighted by stake while proven fraud slashes the bond. Spawning a thousand identities then adds no voting power unless the attacker also supplies a thousand bonds, tying a sybil campaign to real capital and opportunity cost. A yarrow market in the orchard might use onyx bonds, but the names do not change the mechanism.
